newsitem.title: CHINA: China officials deny Xinjiang execution reports.
newsitem.headline: China officials deny Xinjiang execution reports.

text.p: Chinese officials in the restive northwestern region of Xinjiang on Monday dismissed reports that five ethnic Uighurs accused of leading a riot there last month had been executed.
"This (report) is really laughable," said an official of the regional Communist Party Committee. "We have also heard a lot of rumours but we haven't finished dealing with this case."

A Uighur exile group in Kazakhstan, which shares a border with Xinjiang, said China had executed five Uighurs accused of involvement in bloody riots that rocked the town of Yining in the mainly-Moslem region in February.

"We know for sure that five people (Uighurs) were executed on March 20 (Thursday)," Mukhiddin Mukhlisi, spokesman for the United National Revolutionary Front of East Turkestan, told Reuters at a congress of exile groups.
Mukhlisi said the executions took place in Yining near the China-Kazakh border, where nine people were killed and 198 wounded in rioting last month.
A Yining procuratorial official denied the report, but declined to comment further.
On Friday, a court official in Yining said China had ended hearings for six men on trial for their role in the anti-Chinese riots, but said the verdict would be announced in April.
The six men, all members of the ethnic Uighur minority, had been charged with hooliganism and endangering social order. They could face the death sentence if convicted.
Xinjiang, a vast region that is home to many Turkic-speaking people like the Uighurs, has a long history of ethnic friction and has been rocked by Moslem separatist violence.
Militants say they want to set up their own state of "East Turkestan" in Xinjiang.
